title: Hubble views results of NGC 2623 merger
caption: The merging galaxy NGC 2623, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 2623 · constellation Cancer · about 300 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA and A. Evans (Stony Brook University, New York, University of Virginia & National Radio Astronomy Observatory, Charlottesville, USA)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two long tails of young stars stretch out from a single bright center in this Hubble image of NGC 2623. The galaxy is the product of a merger that is now in its late stages, with the cores of the two original galaxies already combined into one nucleus.

When galaxies approach one another, studies show that large amounts of gas are pulled from each toward the other's center, until the pair eventually fuses into one large galaxy. The tidal tails are a strong sign that such a merger has happened, and the violent exchange of gas and mass has set off star formation in both tails.

The lower tail stands out. It is rich in bright star clusters, and 100 of them turned up in these observations. They may have formed in a loop of stretched material linked to the northern tail, or from debris falling back onto the nucleus.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.83 x 1.96 arcminutes) and distance (300 million light years), the frame spans roughly 247,000 × 171,000 light-years. Its light set out about 300 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using a blue filter and a near-infrared filter. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of this data is near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the galaxy is far too faint to see in this detail without a telescope.

explore: Beyond that busy lower tail, both of the galaxy's arms host very young stars that are only in the early stages of their lives. NGC 2623 lies about 300 million light-years away in the constellation Cancer.
alt: A galaxy with a bright central nucleus and two long tails of stars, the lower one dotted with bright star clusters.
